name: Fluconazole
summary: A widely used oral azole antifungal with straightforward dosing and a strong interaction profile because of CYP inhibition.
good: Candida infections where an oral azole is appropriate.
clinicalPearls: It is simple to prescribe but never simple to ignore interaction-wise.
mechanism: Inhibits fungal ergosterol synthesis via lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase inhibition.
indications: Vaginal candidiasis, oral/esophageal candidiasis, and selected systemic fungal infections.
interactionNotes: Warfarin, some statins, sulfonylureas, and other CYP-metabolized drugs can be affected.

warnings: Liver toxicity, QT prolongation, and interaction burden are the main concerns.
